title: Plant Life Cycles and Seeds
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Plant Life Cycles and Seeds Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the life cycle of flowering plants; explain pollination and the conditions seeds need to germinate; describe ways that seeds are dispersed. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Growth and Changes in Plants)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on plant life cycles, germination, flowers and pollination, and how seeds are spread. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Seeds grow into plants that make new seeds.
key_sub: Pollination makes seeds; wind, water and animals spread them.
body_html:
How to think about it

A flowering plant's life cycle: seed → seedling → adult plant → flower → fruit and seeds.

  • Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.
  • Pollination moves pollen from flower to flower, often by bees, butterflies or wind.
  • Seeds spread by wind (maple keys), animals (burrs, berries), water and bursting pods.
Example

How are dandelion seeds spread?

light and fluffy

Answer: by the wind

Example

What do seeds need to germinate?

they start in the soil

Answer: water, air and warmth

Common mistakes

  • Thinking seeds need light to germinate.
  • Thinking only bees pollinate.
  • Thinking a fruit is not part of the plant's life cycle.
